changedBeliefs: Focused AOT harnesses can carry a memory reading, and the instrument is fixed by a hard constraint rather than chosen: an AOT binary exposes no VM service (`Service.getInfo()` returns null, `--enable-vm-service` is rejected as an unrecognized flag), so heap statistics and allocation profiles are unavailable in the only mode exp 193 permits for decode-path results. `ProcessInfo` is the whole instrument, and a `currentRss` read costs ~700 ns so it must stay outside the stopwatch.

`maxRss` and a sampled `currentRss` peak can give opposite verdicts on the same change, by 76 percentage points. Pre- vs post-exp-260 on a lane crossing `sacrificeSlotThreshold`: sampled `currentRss` peak 36.6 -> 64.0 MB (+75%), `maxRss` 65.9 -> 64.8 MB (-1.7%). `maxRss` is the true high-water and is what a guard should gate on; the `currentRss` curve is a retention signal, and retention moves when reader isolates are sacrificed and return their pages. Within one isolate the VM keeps pages after GC, so a candidate freeing its own garbage reads as no change.

Exp 260's memory claim was refuted by measurement in the favourable direction. Its arithmetic predicted peak capacity could rise 22-25% for a result landing just under a doubling boundary; measured peak RSS falls on every lane (-2.1% at 200k slots, -11.5% on the canonical product row, -28.0% on the sub-threshold integer lane). The arithmetic was correct about the buffer and wrong about the read: the buffer is a small part of what a read holds, and the doubling sequence's retained intermediate arrays are a larger one.

Peak read-path memory has been flat for three months. Eight checkpoints from v0.3.0 (2026-05-03) through exp 259 (2026-08-03) hold every lane within ~1 MB, across roughly forty merged experiments including the entire transfer-shape arc (174, 234, 236, 243, 244, 245, 246), while wall time on the same runs fell 25-40%. There is no memory regression to find, and that is now established rather than assumed.

The guard's sensitivity is bounded by that same flatness: four months of experiments moving wall time 25-40% moved peak RSS under 1%. It is a tripwire for a doubling, not an instrument for a 5% drift. It is further diluted by setup — `mixed6-10k` sits at 89.5 MB before the measured reads begin and the reads add ~18 MB — so a lane meant to gate memory should seed as little as it can.

claims.text: A focused-harness memory guard must gate on `ProcessInfo.maxRss` with one process per lane, not on a sampled `currentRss` peak. The two disagreed by 76 percentage points about the same change (sampled peak +75%, `maxRss` -1.7%) on a lane whose results cross `sacrificeSlotThreshold`, because sacrificed isolates return pages and make `currentRss` a retention signal rather than a high-water. Repeatability across five isolated runs per arm is <=0.6 MB, mechanically inert lanes read identical across arms, and sampling moves wall time 1.3-2.4%, inside the 3% floor.
claims.conditions: M1 Pro · AOT CLI bundle · one process per lane · 2026-08

claims.text: Exp 260 lowers peak RSS rather than raising it: `maxRss` falls -2.1% on 10k x 20 INTEGER, -11.5% on the canonical 6-column product row at 10k rows, and -28.0% on 5k x 4 INTEGER, with the point-read control flat at -0.3%. This supersedes the arithmetic in claim 260.4, which predicted peak capacity could rise 22-25% for results landing just under a doubling boundary.
claims.conditions: M1 Pro · AOT · maxRss, one process per lane, 21 samples · 2026-08

claims.text: Peak read-path memory was flat within ~1 MB from v0.3.0 (2026-05-03) to exp 259 (2026-08-03) across eight checkpoints and roughly forty merged experiments, including the whole transfer-shape arc, while wall time on the same runs fell 25-40%. The only movement in the window is exps 259 and 260, both downward. No memory regression has accumulated.
claims.conditions: M1 Pro · AOT · harness source held constant, rebuilt per checkpoint · maxRss, one process per lane · 2026-08

claims.text: `select()` holds far more than its payload: `mixed6-10k` reads a table containing roughly 1.5 MB of data and peaks at 95 MB, and 89.5 MB of the pre-exp-260 figure is resident before the measured reads begin. The ~60x ratio has never been decomposed, and exps 008/032's lazy and facade result shapes were assessed against wall time rather than against this.
claims.conditions: M1 Pro · AOT · maxRss and post-warmup resident, one process per lane · 2026-08

nextSignals: `benchmark/shared/memory_probe.dart` is the memory lane for any focused harness. Start it after seeding and warmup, sample outside the stopwatch, run with `--lane=` so `maxRss` is per-lane clean, and read `lane_isolated` before comparing two runs' `max_rss_mb`.

Do not gate on `rss_growth_mb` or `rss_peak_mb`. They are retention signals and can report a large regression on a change that leaves the high-water untouched — claim 261.1 is the counterexample that established this.

The release-suite Memory stage is `[15/16]`, the exact stage where the sqlite_async peer segfaults, and #282's per-repeat artifact writing does not help because the crash lands inside repeat 1. Persisting each scenario as it completes, rather than each repeat, would preserve the fourteen scenarios that currently die with it — that is the reason trend data is thin, and it gates the `per-benchmark RSS acceptance criteria` candidate that has been open since 2026-05-02.

The next memory question worth a run is claim 261.4's ~60x payload-to-peak ratio on `select()`, decomposed rather than assumed. That needs allocation counters at specific sites, not process RSS, because the guard cannot resolve anything below a doubling.
